title: My Son?
paragraphs: The cart-driver holding on the Mayilai bullocks and saying “We’ve arrived at Karuṇaiyānanta Press”, Kaliyaperumāḷ leaning comfortably in the cart, alighted with a bag in his hands.
As soon as Kaliyaperumāḷ entered the room of the manager in the frontier of the printing press, he was greeted by the saluting manager with the chants of “Welcome! Welcome!” and was offered a chair.
Kaliyaperumāḷ extricated five or six big papers from his bag and said, “An auspicious event is slated to take place in our house. That is why I have come here.”
“I am very happy. Seems like son’s marriage. You are here for printing invitation. Went through the news!”

“Yes, the marriage was fixed in a hurry. One thousand invitations must be printed. Groom’s name - Bride’s name and other details are there in these papers! You yourself can make necessary corrections.”

The manager scanned through the papers handed to him and remarked, “Okay! Though it is a self-respect marriage, the Ayyar who wrote this seems to have smeared customary turmeric powder on it and noted down the auspicious time for marriage along with astrological details as in the conventional marriage.”

“Is that so? Has he written the auspicious time? The Ayyar has shown his true colours! It is okay. Though the Ayyar has set an auspicious time for the marriage, it would be conducted on line with the principles of Periyar. Therefore, let the title of the invitation be ‘Wedding Celebration Invitation’.”
“If it is a self-respect marriage, then why are you sticking to auspicious date and stars?”

“Don’t you know? On certain occasions, vedic rituals would be insisted upon by bridegroom’s side, whereas, at times, bride’s side would take turns to sticking to them. Here, for the sake of the bride’s family - the astrological details. And in accordance with our wish, self-respect marriage.”

The manager smiled and scrutinized the marriage invitation given to him by Kaliyaperumāḷ for printing. “Is everything okay? Do you know as to why I am asking this? You possess proficiency in Tamil with a knack of rectifying even minor mistakes! That is why we prefer this press!”
“Everything is correct except for one mistake!”
“What is it?”
“Not exactly a big mistake. While writing bridegroom’s name, you have mentioned it as ‘my son’ (eṉatu makaṉ).”
“Yes, the bridegroom is my son...”
“Sir, that is exactly the mistake.”
“What are you saying, Meyyappaṉ? He is my son, otherwise, who else is he?”
“That is not correct.”
“You give back that paper! What blabbering is this?”
Kaliyaperumāḷ snatched the paper from the hands of Meyyappaṉ. Just then, Meyyappaṉ caught hold of his hand and pleaded:
“My apologies. You only commended my Tamil proficiency, then how come you get agitated?”
“Okay; What do you want to say? Speak out!”
“The sixth case marker atu in eṉatu makaṉ is wrong. We must use the fourth case marker ku and write eṉakku makaṉ.”
“I hardly know anything about case markers and distinctions of human and non-human classes. Because you say this, it must be correct.”
“I don’t say that! Tolkāppiyam states so!”
“Whosoever might say so, there is no denying the fact that he is my son! Kindly finish the invitation printing work soon. And here is your advance amount. Now, let me take your leave.”

> Where the succeeding word > Is the human generic class [kinship denoting] noun, > The sixth case declension atu of the preceding word > Gets dropped, > And the fourth case morpheme ku takes its place. > > (Collatikāram: Vēṟṟumai Mayaṅkiyal, verse 11)
